mcq.q: Photosynthesis in the vine’s leaves produces
choices: A Only colour compounds for the skins
B Sugars that later become alcohol in the berry
C Tannin in the seeds before veraison
mcq.answer: B Sugars that later become alcohol in the berry
mcq.why: Chlorophyll uses light to make sugar; that sugar is the fermentable material.

mcq.q: A Mediterranean climate is characterised by
choices: A Rain evenly in every month, including harvest
B Dry summers and most rain in winter
C Constant fog and no sunshine
D Arctic winters and no vines
mcq.answer: B Dry summers and most rain in winter
mcq.why: Warm, dry growing seasons; winter rain stores water in the soil.

mcq.q: Phylloxera is managed in most vineyards by
choices: B Grafting Vitis vinifera onto resistant rootstocks
C Flooding every row each summer
D Planting only on pure sand is never used
mcq.answer: B Grafting Vitis vinifera onto resistant rootstocks
mcq.why: Resistant American rootstocks are the standard defence; a few sandy sites remain ungrafted.

mcq.q: Green harvesting means
choices: A Picking only underripe fruit for acidity
B Dropping bunches before ripening so the vine finishes a smaller crop
C Harvesting at night by machine
mcq.answer: B Dropping bunches before ripening so the vine finishes a smaller crop
mcq.why: Yield is cut after fruit set so remaining bunches ripen more fully.

mcq.q: Chaptalisation is the addition of
choices: A Tartaric acid to a hot-climate must
B Sugar (or must concentrate) before or during ferment to raise potential alcohol
mcq.answer: B Sugar (or must concentrate) before or during ferment to raise potential alcohol
mcq.why: Allowed in cooler regions; it raises alcohol, not residual sweetness if the wine ferments dry.

mcq.q: Most quality red wines undergo malolactic conversion in order to
choices: A Keep malic bite and prevent any texture
B Soften acidity and add microbiological stability
mcq.answer: B Soften acidity and add microbiological stability
mcq.why: Almost all reds go through MLF; many rich whites do too.

mcq.q: Press wine from a red fermenter, compared with free-run, is usually
choices: A Paler and lower in tannin
B Darker and higher in tannin
C Sweet and low in alcohol
mcq.answer: B Darker and higher in tannin
mcq.why: Harder press fractions pull more skin and seed tannin.

mcq.q: A reductive handling of a white wine aims to
choices: A Expose the must to as much air as possible
B Limit oxygen so primary fruit is kept
mcq.answer: B Limit oxygen so primary fruit is kept
mcq.why: Inert gas, cool temperatures and SO2 protect thiols and esters.

mcq.q: Entre-Deux-Mers is an appellation for
choices: B Dry white wines, mainly Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon
mcq.answer: B Dry white wines, mainly Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon
mcq.why: The name on a bottle is a dry white AOC between Garonne and Dordogne.

mcq.q: Sauternes and Barsac need noble rot, which requires
choices: A Constant drought and no humidity
B Humid mornings and dry, sunny afternoons
mcq.answer: B Humid mornings and dry, sunny afternoons
mcq.why: Mist from the Ciron/Garonne then sun: Botrytis cinerea as noble rot, not grey rot.

mcq.q: Côte Chalonnaise villages such as Mercurey and Rully produce
choices: B Pinot Noir and Chardonnay in a similar vein to the Côte d’Or, usually at lower price
mcq.answer: B Pinot Noir and Chardonnay in a similar vein to the Côte d’Or, usually at lower price
mcq.why: South of the Côte d’Or: same grapes, slightly cooler/less famous sites.

mcq.q: Pouilly-Fuissé comes from the
choices: B Mâconnais and is a Chardonnay appellation
mcq.answer: B Mâconnais and is a Chardonnay appellation
mcq.why: Warmest Burgundy Chardonnay zone; riper stone fruit than Chablis.

mcq.q: Muscadet Sèvre-et-Maine sur lie must be bottled
choices: A After three years in new oak
B From the lees, which adds a slight yeastiness and sometimes a prickle
C As a sweet late-harvest wine
mcq.answer: B From the lees, which adds a slight yeastiness and sometimes a prickle
mcq.why: Sur lie is the local quality cue: lees contact, early bottling, freshness.

mcq.q: Vouvray can be dry, off-dry, sweet or sparkling because
choices: A The AOC allows only Sauvignon Blanc
B Chenin Blanc holds acid even at high ripeness, so residual sugar is a stylistic choice
mcq.answer: B Chenin Blanc holds acid even at high ripeness, so residual sugar is a stylistic choice
mcq.why: Chenin’s acid is the frame; demi-sec and moelleux are classic.

mcq.q: Côte-Rôtie may include a small proportion of
choices: A Marsanne in a separate white cuvée only
mcq.answer: B Viognier co-fermented with Syrah
mcq.why: Up to a legal maximum of Viognier can be co-fermented; it lifts aroma.

mcq.q: Cornas is
choices: B A 100% Syrah AOC, often the ripest of the Northern Rhône reds
D A rosé-only AOC like Tavel
mcq.answer: B A 100% Syrah AOC, often the ripest of the Northern Rhône reds
mcq.why: Sheltered amphitheatre; all Syrah; sturdy and dark.

mcq.q: Tavel is an appellation for
choices: B Rosé only, from Southern Rhône grapes
mcq.answer: B Rosé only, from Southern Rhône grapes
mcq.why: Tavel is dry, relatively deep rosé; Lirac next door makes red, white and rosé.

mcq.q: Alsace Pinot Gris, compared with Italian Pinot Grigio, is often
choices: A Lighter, sharper and always sparkling
B Fuller, more textured, and may have some residual sugar
D A red wine from free-run juice
mcq.answer: B Fuller, more textured, and may have some residual sugar
mcq.why: Alsace PG is a noble variety here: weight, spice, and sometimes sweetness.

mcq.q: Barbaresco, next to Barolo, is also made from
mcq.answer: C Nebbiolo
mcq.why: Same grape; often slightly earlier-ripening sites and a shorter legal ageing.

mcq.q: Vino Nobile di Montepulciano is based on
choices: A Montepulciano the grape, grown in Abruzzo
B Sangiovese (locally Prugnolo Gentile) in Tuscany
mcq.answer: B Sangiovese (locally Prugnolo Gentile) in Tuscany
mcq.why: The town of Montepulciano uses Sangiovese; the grape Montepulciano is a different variety.

mcq.q: Soave Classico, compared with basic Soave, usually comes from
choices: A The fertile Po valley floor only
B Hill sites in the historic zone, often with more concentration
mcq.answer: B Hill sites in the historic zone, often with more concentration
mcq.why: Classico is the hills around Soave and Monteforte; Garganega again.

mcq.q: Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi is a
choices: B Dry white from the Marche with high acid and a bitter-almond note
mcq.answer: B Dry white from the Marche with high acid and a bitter-almond note
mcq.why: Marche’s flagship white; can age; not Pinot Grigio.

mcq.q: Priorat reds are typically
choices: B High-alcohol, low-yield Garnacha and Cariñena from llicorella slopes
mcq.answer: B High-alcohol, low-yield Garnacha and Cariñena from llicorella slopes
mcq.why: Old bush vines, steep costers, very low yields, concentrated reds.

mcq.q: Rías Baixas benefits from
choices: A A hot continental plateau like Ribera
B A cool, wet Atlantic climate suited to Albariño
mcq.answer: B A cool, wet Atlantic climate suited to Albariño
mcq.why: Galicia’s rain and coast keep the wines crisp; canopy work fights rot.

mcq.q: A Rioja Reserva red, compared with a Joven, will typically show more
choices: A Fresh banana from carbonic maceration
B Developed strawberry, vanilla and spice from longer oak and bottle age
mcq.answer: B Developed strawberry, vanilla and spice from longer oak and bottle age
mcq.why: Reserva: 3 years minimum, ≥1 in oak; American oak is a Rioja tradition.

mcq.q: Mosel Riesling Kabinett is typically
choices: A High alcohol, low acid, heavily oaked
B Light in body and alcohol, high in acid, often with some residual sugar
C A red wine from Pinot Noir
mcq.answer: B Light in body and alcohol, high in acid, often with some residual sugar
mcq.why: Steep slate, cool sites, and a light Prädikat: the classic delicate Mosel.

mcq.q: Grüner Veltliner is the leading grape of
choices: B The Danube regions of Austria (Wachau, Kremstal, Kamptal)
mcq.answer: B The Danube regions of Austria (Wachau, Kremstal, Kamptal)
mcq.why: White pepper, citrus and lentil; Smaragd/Federspiel in the Wachau.

mcq.q: Vinho Verde’s Alvarinho is concentrated around
choices: B Monção and Melgaço, near the Minho river
mcq.answer: B Monção and Melgaço, near the Minho river
mcq.why: The northern sub-region gives the ripest, most serious Alvarinho.

mcq.q: Alentejo, compared with Vinho Verde, generally produces reds that are
choices: A Lighter, sharper and slightly sparkling
B Riper, fuller and from a warmer, drier inland climate
mcq.answer: B Riper, fuller and from a warmer, drier inland climate
mcq.why: Alentejo is warm plains: Alicante Bouschet, Aragonez, Trincadeira, plus internationals.

mcq.q: Russian River Valley and Sonoma Coast are Californian sources of
choices: B Pinot Noir and Chardonnay in cooler, often foggy sites
mcq.answer: B Pinot Noir and Chardonnay in cooler, often foggy sites
mcq.why: Pacific fog and breeze keep these AVAs cooler than inland Napa.

mcq.q: The Uco Valley in Mendoza is prized because
choices: A It is at sea level and very humid
B Higher altitude gives cooler nights and a longer season for Malbec and whites
C It is Chile’s coastal plain
D It produces only fortified wines
mcq.answer: B Higher altitude gives cooler nights and a longer season for Malbec and whites
mcq.why: Uco sits higher than Luján/Maipú; freshness and floral Malbec.

mcq.q: Hunter Valley Semillon, when bottled young and aged in bottle, typically becomes
choices: A Heavy, sweet and oaked like a barrique Chardonnay
B A low-alcohol, waxy, toast-and-honey wine from a humid region
mcq.answer: B A low-alcohol, waxy, toast-and-honey wine from a humid region
mcq.why: Picked early, little oak, then bottle age does the work — a local classic.

mcq.q: Hawke’s Bay’s Gimblett Gravels are known for
choices: B Bordeaux blends and Syrah on free-draining warm gravels
mcq.answer: B Bordeaux blends and Syrah on free-draining warm gravels
mcq.why: Warm stones, low vigour: New Zealand’s most serious Cabernet/Merlot and Syrah.

mcq.q: A German wine labelled Trocken is
choices: A Always a TBA-level sweet wine
mcq.answer: B Dry, regardless of Prädikat
mcq.why: Trocken states dryness of the finished wine; a Spätlese can be trocken.

mcq.q: DOCG is Italy’s
choices: B Most tightly controlled PDO tier, above DOC
C Name for table wine with no origin
D Term for organic grapes only
mcq.answer: B Most tightly controlled PDO tier, above DOC
mcq.why: Denominazione di Origine Controllata e Garantita sits above DOC.

mcq.q: If an EU still wine names a single variety, at least this share must be that variety
mcq.why: 85% is the EU default (stricter local rules can apply).

mcq.q: Pinot Meunier is valued in Champagne blends because it
choices: A Gives the most longevity of the three grapes
B Ripens more easily and adds early fruit, useful in cooler sites
C Must be used for all vintage wines
D Is the only grape of the Côte des Blancs
mcq.answer: B Ripens more easily and adds early fruit, useful in cooler sites
mcq.why: Meunier is the reliable, fruity partner; Chardonnay and Pinot Noir give more age.

mcq.q: The liqueur d’expédition is added
choices: A To start the first alcoholic ferment
B After disgorgement to set the sweetness (dosage)
C To feed flor in a solera
D Instead of the tirage yeast
mcq.answer: B After disgorgement to set the sweetness (dosage)
mcq.why: Dosage wine + sugar after the lees are ejected; Brut Nature has little or none.

mcq.q: Franciacorta is
choices: A A tank-method Glera wine from Veneto
B A traditional-method DOCG from Lombardy, mainly Chardonnay and Pinot
mcq.answer: B A traditional-method DOCG from Lombardy, mainly Chardonnay and Pinot
mcq.why: Italy’s most serious bottle-fermented sparkling; longer lees than basic Prosecco.

mcq.q: Sekt on a German label may be made by
choices: A Only the traditional method in one village
B Tank or traditional method, and quality varies widely
mcq.answer: B Tank or traditional method, and quality varies widely
mcq.why: Winzersekt is the grower, often bottle-fermented, end; much Sekt is tank and bulk.

mcq.q: A wine labelled Extra Dry (Extra Sec) is
choices: B Sweeter than Brut, about 12–17 g/L
D A synonym for Brut Nature
mcq.answer: B Sweeter than Brut, about 12–17 g/L
mcq.why: The name is misleading: Extra Dry sits above Brut on the sugar scale.

mcq.q: Amontillado Sherry has been aged
choices: A Only under flor from start to bottling
B First under flor, then oxidatively after the flor is lost
C Only in bottle like Vintage Port
mcq.answer: B First under flor, then oxidatively after the flor is lost
mcq.why: The two-stage life gives a darker, nuttier wine than Fino, drier than Cream.

mcq.q: White Port is made from
choices: B White Douro varieties, fortified during fermentation
mcq.answer: B White Douro varieties, fortified during fermentation
mcq.why: Malvasia, Viosinho and others; styles from dry to sweet; often an aperitif over ice.

mcq.q: Colheita Port is
choices: B A single-vintage tawny, aged in wood for many years
C A rosé Port drunk from the tank
D Another name for crusted Port
mcq.answer: B A single-vintage tawny, aged in wood for many years
mcq.why: Vintage date + long oxidative wood: a dated tawny, not a bottle-aged vintage.

mcq.q: Banyuls and Maury are
choices: B Roussillon vins doux naturels, often from Grenache Noir
mcq.answer: B Roussillon vins doux naturels, often from Grenache Noir
mcq.why: Fortified mid-ferment; can be oxidative or more youthful and fruity.

mcq.q: Madeira’s estufagem process uses
choices: B Artificial heat to mature the wine faster
C Ice crystals to concentrate must
mcq.answer: B Artificial heat to mature the wine faster
mcq.why: Estufagem heats cheaper Madeira; canteiro (cask in a warm loft) is gentler for quality.

mcq.q: Reduction on the nose (for example rotten egg) is due to
choices: B Volatile sulphur compounds such as H2S
mcq.answer: B Volatile sulphur compounds such as H2S
mcq.why: Low oxygen and stressed yeast produce sulphides; some blow off, some do not.

mcq.q: Light red wines such as Beaujolais or Loire Cabernet Franc are often served
choices: C Ice-cold in a champagne bucket until 4 °C
mcq.answer: B Slightly cool, about 12–14 °C
mcq.why: A light chill keeps fruit tight; room heat makes them soupy.

mcq.q: Umami-rich dishes (soy, mushrooms, ripe tomato) tend to make a high-tannin red taste
choices: C Much higher in residual sugar
mcq.answer: B More bitter and metallic
mcq.why: Umami exaggerates tannin bitterness; choose lower tannin or add fat/salt with care.

mcq.q: A wine described on the SAT as ‘can drink now, but has potential for ageing’ is
choices: B Ready, yet still improving in bottle
D Unsuitable for any further age
mcq.answer: B Ready, yet still improving in bottle
mcq.why: Four readiness options: too young; now but will age; now, not for ageing; too old.

parts.prompt: Describe the climates of Anjou-Saumur and Touraine and how they affect Chenin Blanc ripeness and style.
points: Cool-moderate maritime climate; Atlantic influence fades inland; vintage variation.
Anjou: warmer, drier in places (schist in Savennières; Coteaux du Layon botrytis valleys).
Touraine / Vouvray: tuffeau limestone and a slightly more continental touch; frost and rain still matter.
Chenin keeps high acid even when ripe, so dry, off-dry and sweet wines are all possible.
Noble rot in sheltered Layon/Quarts de Chaume; dry wines on windier slopes (Savennières).
Harvest may be in tries (successive passes) for sweet wines.

parts.prompt: Compare Savennières with Coteaux du Layon (or Quarts de Chaume) and with Vouvray.
points: Savennières: dry, full, often austere in youth, schist, long-lived.
Coteaux du Layon / Quarts de Chaume / Bonnezeaux: sweet, botrytis or passerillage, high acid keeps them fresh.
Vouvray: the full range — sec, demi-sec, moelleux, plus traditional-method sparkling.
Name grapes: Chenin Blanc (Pineau de la Loire).
Soil contrast: Anjou schist vs Touraine tuffeau can score.
Do not invent AOCs.

parts.prompt: Outline winery choices for a dry Savennières and for a sweet Layon.
points: Dry: healthy fruit, press, settle, ferment (tank and/or old oak) to dryness; MLF optional/rare; lees for texture; modest new oak.
Sweet: selected botrytis fruit, gentle press, slow ferment that stops with residual sugar (cold, SO2, or yeast stall); no need to chaptalise if ripe.
Both keep Chenin’s acid; avoid heavy new oak on delicate sweet wines.
Ageing: dry wines in bottle for years; sweet wines even longer.
Sparkling Vouvray as a third path can score if clearly labelled as such.

written.title: Question 2 — Rioja and Ribera del Duero

parts.prompt: Compare climate and vineyard conditions in Rioja with those in Ribera del Duero.
points: Rioja: Atlantic, Mediterranean and continental influences; Rioja Alta / Alavesa cooler and wetter, Oriental (Baja) warmer and drier.
Ribera: higher plateau, more extreme continental (hot days, cold nights, frost, short season).
Both: Tempranillo (Tinto Fino / Tinta del País in Ribera).
Rioja allows Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuelo; Ribera is more Tempranillo-dominant, some Cabernet/Merlot.
Altitude and the Duero river vs Ebro basin.
Harvest frost and spring frost risk higher in Ribera.

parts.prompt: Explain Rioja’s ageing categories and how American oak has shaped the traditional style.
points: Joven / generic: little or no oak requirement.
Crianza: 2 years, ≥1 year oak (red).
Reserva: 3 years, ≥1 year oak.
Gran Reserva: 5 years, ≥2 years oak.
American oak: coconut, vanilla, dill; traditional bodegas; French oak now common for a tighter style.
Bottle age is part of the legal total for Reserva/GR.
White/rosé have shorter minima (if mentioned, can score).

parts.prompt: Describe typical winemaking for a structured Ribera del Duero tinto versus a traditional Reserva Rioja.
points: Ribera: riper fruit, deeper colour, more extraction, often French barriques, fuller body, firmer tannin.
Traditional Rioja: long American-oak ageing, more oxidative evolution, softer tannin, brick rim, developed fruit.
Both: destem, skin ferment, MLF, racking.
Modern Rioja can look more like Ribera (less time, French oak).
Yield and altitude as quality levers.
Name a style outcome: plush dark fruit vs strawberry-and-vanilla.

parts.prompt: Name three traditional-method sparkling wines from outside Champagne and state grape(s) and region for each.
points: Cava (Catalonia / designated Spanish zones): Macabeo, Xarel-lo, Parellada ± Chardonnay/Pinot.
Crémant de Loire / Bourgogne / Alsace / Limoux: local grapes (Chenin, Pinot, Chardonnay, Auxerrois, Mauzac, etc.).
Franciacorta (Lombardy): Chardonnay, Pinot Nero, Pinot Bianco.
English sparkling (South/South-East): Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Meunier on chalk/greensand.
Cap Classique (South Africa), New World (California, Australia, New Zealand) as further examples.
One mark per accurate named wine + grapes + place, up to 9.

parts.prompt: Which parts of the traditional method stay the same, and which choices most affect style?
points: Same: second ferment in bottle, lees ageing, riddling, disgorgement, dosage.
Base-wine climate and ripeness set acid and fruit (cooler = leaner).
Variety and blend (BdB vs BdN).
Oak vs tank for the base wine.
Time on lees (autolysis).
Dosage level (Brut Nature to Demi-sec).
Reserve wine and malolactic as further levers.
Press fractions (cuvée vs taille).

parts.prompt: Why can cool-climate England produce high-acid traditional-method wines, and what is a vineyard risk?
points: High latitude, cool season, chalk or limestone in key counties: grapes stay high in acid, modest in sugar — ideal for sparkling base wines.
Climate change has improved ripening reliability.
Risks: spring frost, rain at flowering and harvest, rot, vintage variation.
Low yields and high cost.
Award for naming a county (Sussex, Kent, Hampshire) without inventing an AOC.

written.title: Question 4 — Food, service and German Riesling

parts.prompt: State the SAT structural components that matter most when matching wine to food, and give one food effect for acidity, sweetness, tannin and alcohol.
points: Acidity: refreshed by salt and fat; makes food taste cleaner; sour food needs equal or higher acid in the wine.
Sweetness: food sweetness makes dry wine taste thinner; match or exceed the dish’s sugar.
Tannin: softened by protein and fat; increased by chilli and umami.
Alcohol: heat clashes with chilli and with very sweet or very light dishes; high alcohol can taste hot with spice.
Body and flavour intensity should be in the same register as the dish.
Acid + bubbles cut fried food.

parts.prompt: Recommend a Mosel Kabinett Riesling for a spicy south-east Asian dish. Justify service temperature and residual sugar.
points: Off-dry or kabinett-level RS cools chilli; high acid keeps the wine from cloying.
Low alcohol (often 8–9%) does not fan the heat.
Serve well chilled (about 7–10 °C).
Aromatic citrus/floral notes sit with herbs and lime.
A dry Grosses Gewächs would be less kind to chilli.
Do not serve at red-wine temperature.

parts.prompt: How should a half-finished bottle of that Riesling be stored, and when should it be drunk?
points: Recork, refrigerate, upright; drink within a few days (aromatic whites fade).
Keep away from light and heat.
A screwcap helps but does not stop flavour loss once opened.
Do not store in a warm kitchen.
Unopened: cool, dark, steady; off-dry Riesling can age, but a cheap kabinett is for early drinking.
Freezing or a sunny windowsill are both wrong.
